description: An infinite canvas you and the agent share: cards of Markdown, files and links, groups and arrows between them. Sketch an architecture, plan a feature, map a codebase, or ask the agent to lay something out. Saved as .canvas files (JSON Canvas, the open format Obsidian uses). Bundled to try: turn it on, or uninstall it.

commands.title: Canvas: Open
commands.description: Opens a canvas (a .canvas file) beside the editor, creating it when missing. Input: { path?: string } (default: the project's main canvas, <workspace folder>/canvas/main.canvas). Returns { path }.

commands.title: Canvas: New canvas
commands.description: Creates an empty canvas and opens it. Input: { path?: string } (default: a new file in <workspace folder>/canvas). Returns { path }.

commands.title: Canvas: New canvas…
commands.description: Asks for a name and creates that canvas (in the canvas folder, or at a path with a /), then opens it. For the user; agents use canvas.new with a path.

commands.title: Canvas: Read
commands.description: What's on a canvas: its cards (id, type text/file/link/group, x, y, width, height, color, and text / file / url / label), its arrows (id, from, to, label) and the cards the user has selected in it. Input: { path?: string }. Read it before changing a canvas the user worked on.

commands.title: Canvas: Edit
commands.description: Changes a canvas the user can see, in one step (it opens beside the editor and the changed cards light up). Input: { path?: string, reveal?: boolean (default true), ops: [...] }, applied in order. Ops: {op:'add', type?:'text'|'file'|'link'|'group', text?: Markdown, file?: workspace path, url?, label?, color?: '1'..'6' (red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, purple) or '#hex', ref?: a name later ops in the same call can use instead of an id, near?: id or ref to place it next to, side?: 'right'|'below'|'left'|'above', x?, y?, width?, height?} (no position: placed in free space; no size: fitted to the text); {op:'update', id, ...fields}; {op:'remove', ids}; {op:'connect', from, to, label?, color?, fromSide?, toSide?, toEnd?: 'arrow'|'none'}; {op:'disconnect', ids?: edge ids, from?, to?}; {op:'group', ids, label?} (a group around those cards); {op:'layout', style: 'tree'|'grid'|'row'|'column', ids?} (tree follows the arrows left to right); {op:'clear'}. Returns { path, added: {ref or index: id}, changed, removed }.

commands.title: Canvas: Show cards
commands.description: Opens a canvas and zooms to cards so the user sees them. Input: { path?: string, ids?: string[] } (no ids: everything).

commands.title: Canvas: List canvases
commands.description: The .canvas files in the project's canvas folder and at the top of the project. Returns { canvases: string[] }.

commands.title: Canvas: Refresh the list
commands.description: Looks for the project's canvases again (the Canvases view).

commands.title: Canvas: Add to canvas
commands.description: Puts file cards on the canvas in use (else the main canvas): a file, or a folder's files. Input: { path?: string, paths?: string[] }.

commands.title: Canvas: Export as image
commands.description: Saves a picture of a canvas next to it (opening it if needed). Input: { path?, format?: 'png'|'svg' (default png), area?: 'all'|'view', scale?: 1|2|3 (PNG, default 2), privacy?: boolean (grey bars instead of text) }. Returns { path } of the image.

canvas.snapToGrid.description: Cards snap to a 20 px grid when you move or resize them.

canvas.showGrid.description: Show a dot grid behind the cards.

canvas.folder.description: Where new canvases go and the Canvases list looks first, relative to the project. Empty: canvas in the IDE's own workspace folder; a .vscode or legacy canvas folder is listed too.

canvas.cardWidth.description: Width of a new card, in pixels.

canvas.arrowStyle.description: How arrows are drawn: curved, straight, or elbow (right angles).

canvas.showImages.description: Show images on image file cards (off: just their names, for very large images).

canvas.embedPages.description: Show web pages inside link cards (YouTube and Vimeo as players). Some sites refuse to be shown inside another page: use the card's Show as a link.

canvas.snapToObjects.description: While you move cards, line them up with other cards' edges and centres (guides show where). Hold Space to move freely.
